questions.question: What does a map legend explain?
choices: The meaning of symbols and colors
The exact population of every city
The history of every border
The age of the paper

questions.question: What does a map scale show?
choices: The height of every mountain
The number of countries in the world
The relationship between map distance and real-world distance
The date of every road's construction

questions.question: What does a compass rose indicate?
choices: Population density
Directions
Rainfall totals
Political party strength

questions.question: What does a physical map emphasize?
choices: Election results only
City voting districts only
Trade prices only
Landforms and other natural features

questions.question: What does a political map emphasize?
choices: Boundaries and political units
Elevation contours only
Rainfall averages only
Types of bedrock only

questions.question: What do contour lines connect on a topographic map?
choices: Places with the same population
Cities founded in the same year
Points of equal elevation
Roads with equal traffic

questions.question: What is a thematic map?
choices: A map that always shows every feature
A map focused on a particular subject or pattern
A map without symbols
A map drawn only from memory

questions.question: Why do flat world maps involve distortion?
choices: Maps must always omit all oceans
Every projection uses inaccurate measurements deliberately
Latitude and longitude cannot be represented on paper
Earth's curved surface cannot be flattened without changing some properties

questions.question: What do closely spaced contour lines generally indicate?
choices: A steep slope
A broad flat plain
A higher population
A national border

questions.question: Why might an equal-area projection be chosen?
choices: To preserve every distance and direction at once
To remove the need for a map legend
To compare relative sizes of regions more accurately
To show all mountains at their true height

questions.question: Why should a reader check a map's date?
choices: Old maps always contain no useful evidence
Borders, roads, and other mapped information may change
Map scale changes only with calendar years
Every map expires after one month

questions.question: Why should a choropleth map of population density use a rate rather than total population?
choices: Totals and density always mean the same thing
Rates remove every need for geographic context
Total population is impossible to measure
Rates allow comparison while accounting for different area sizes

questions.question: What does a map inset often provide?
choices: A closer view or location context for part of a map
A guarantee that no projection distortion exists
A complete written history of each settlement
A replacement for every symbol in the legend

questions.question: Why is a map a selective representation?
choices: Every map includes every possible feature
Only physical maps omit details
Its purpose and scale determine which details are included
All maps must show identical information

questions.question: Why can straight-line distance differ from travel distance?
choices: Travel distance is always shorter than straight-line distance
Routes may follow roads and terrain rather than a direct path
Map scale measures only airline tickets
Real-world distances cannot be estimated from maps

questions.question: A scale says 1 centimeter represents 10 kilometers. Two towns are 4 centimeters apart. What is the represented distance?
choices: 4 kilometers
14 kilometers
400 kilometers
40 kilometers

questions.question: Which map is best for planning a route through mountain terrain?
choices: A detailed topographic map
A world map of language families
A national map of election results
A continent map of population totals

questions.question: A reader compares countries' apparent sizes on a world map. What should be checked?
choices: Only the map's font
Only the order of countries in the legend
The projection and its area distortion
The number of colors used for roads

questions.question: A map colors large regions dark because they have many residents. Why might that mislead a reader studying crowding?
choices: Every large region has the same density
High total population does not necessarily mean high population density
Color cannot represent numerical information
Population totals and land area are unrelated to density

questions.question: Two maps of a city show different detail levels. What is the most likely explanation?
choices: One must necessarily be false
Cities have no measurable location
A legend determines the city's actual size
They use different scales or purposes
